A1.justification: Both PDFs describe JetFormer and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–F. The complete material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original JetFormer generation and understanding experiments, component ablations, and additional analyses in Appendices C–D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including ImageNet generation, COCO generation/captioning, VQAv2 evaluation and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: Appendix A changes the specified coupling operation from scaling by exp(a) then shifting to shifting then scaling by sigma(a), with a corresponding inverse. This is a localized model-specification revision; the PDFs do not establish whether implementation changed or the earlier description was corrected.

E1.justification: ImageNet and WebLI training coverage and the generation, classification, captioning and VQAv2 tasks remain unchanged. Appendix D retains the same ImageNet, COCO and TextVQA manipulation examples, without adding domains or test scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged in Tables 1, 3 and 4, as do both VAE-based comparators in Appendix C, Table 7. The newly cited Wave-Tacotron work is not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Tables 5–6 retain the same model sizes, preprocessing, training budgets, fine-tuning settings and evaluation metrics. The added frozen-flow projection detail documents an existing ablation rather than explicitly changing its protocol.

E4.justification: Table 2 and Appendices C–D retain the same component ablations, VAE comparison, noise and training-duration analyses, and image/latent manipulation studies. Clarifying an ablation and relocating Table 8 do not add analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions specify medians of 10 runs for fine-tuning metrics, except VQAv2 test-dev accuracy from the evaluation server, in Appendix A. Repeated-run information and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Reported numerical results, plotted trends and qualitative samples are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains JetFormer-L FID 6.64, and Table 8 retains FID 7.10 and NLL 3.04 after 1000 epochs with the noise curriculum.

T1.justification: Appendix A revises the mathematical definition of the affine coupling map and its inverse, changing the scaling expression and shift placement. The likelihood factorization, dequantization reasoning and Appendix B objective remain unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about end-to-end raw-image/text likelihood modeling, noise-curriculum benefits, competitive generation and image understanding. No contribution or novelty claim changes.

C2.justification: Interpretations of the noise curriculum, latent redundancy and generation/understanding tradeoffs remain unchanged. Section 5 still acknowledges weaker sample quality than leading diffusion models and increased computational requirements.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository pointer on page 1. Section 4.1 also specifies that the existing frozen-flow ablation factors out latent dimensions using a learnable invertible linear map, improving implementation documentation without establishing a rerun.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Weiss et al. (2021), Wave-Tacotron, to the speech-related discussion. Anonymous (2024) becomes Kolesnikov et al. (2024), identifying the same Jet paper rather than adding another work.

P1.justification: Limited edits clarify ablation descriptions, add a Section 3.2 cross-reference, remove redundant wording and update author/header text. The section sequence and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds conference headers and reformats the author block. Appendix B starts on page 17, Table 8 moves from page 17 to 18, and Figure 5 shifts downward. Figure content and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The code pointer and explicit frozen-flow projection detail address small reproducibility gaps in v1. These provide a limited documentation gain while empirical evidence and core claims remain unchanged. The coupling-equation revision leaves unresolved whether it corrects the description or reflects an implementation change.
